# Roadmap — SEC filing-index ingestion

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`).
Choices made: uv workspace of four packages under `packages/` (root `pyproject.toml`).

| # | Outcome | Spec | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Archived quarterly filing indexes for a chosen range, downloaded once into a baseline | §3 R1; §2.1; §4.2 | A | 1 | About 2 SEC requests per quarter (listing plus index), so seconds at 3 req/s for any range (§4.8); bytes per quarter measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | Daily indexes picked up on an ongoing basis, catching up after missed runs | §3 R2; §2.1; §4.2 | A | 2 | About 250 daily files a year plus listings (one per business day); request time negligible at 3 req/s |
| O3 | Downloaded indexes turned into a canonical filing-index table in Parquet | §3 R3; §4.5; §4.6 | A | 3 | Parse time and memory per quarter measured by Stage 1 |
| O4 | The pipeline running on Azure (ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, Azure Monitor) | §3 R4; §4.1; §4.9 | A | 4 | Azure spend cannot be estimated before resource sizes are chosen; measured by Stage 7's smoke test (§7 step 4) |
| O5 | Backfill, daily ingestion and reconciliation sharing one downloader, parser and publisher | §3 R5; §4.1 | A | 5 | Not material |
| O6 | Original bytes kept, so a parser change reprocesses without re-downloading | §3 R6; §4.3; §4.5 | A | 6 | Storage grows by the raw bytes of every snapshot kept; per-quarter size measured by Stage 1 |
| O7 | The quarterly baseline re-checked on a schedule, with changes recorded | §3 R7; §4.2; §4.4 | A | 7 | About 2 requests per supported quarter per weekly run (§4.8) |
| O8 | All SEC traffic held to one shared request budget, whatever the number of workers | §3 R8; §4.3 | A | 8 | Caps throughput at 3 req/s, about 10,800 requests an hour (§4.8) |
| O9 | Readers get a complete, versioned quarter through one active pointer | §3 R9; §4.5; §4.6 | A | 9 | Not material |
| O10 | Records leave the catalog only with explicit approval tied to a source hash | §3 R10; §4.4 | A | 10 | Your time for each closed-quarter candidate that removes keys |
| O11 | Schedules, retry limits and rate target held as reviewed configuration | §3 R11; §4.8; §5 | A | 11 | Not material |

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

Order diverges from the ranking where a dependency requires it. O3 joins O1 in Stage 1, because a baseline that is not parsed is not a usable result. O6 (manifest and replay) and O9 (publication) come before O2, because daily ingestion consumes both. O8 follows O2, because the budget only becomes shared once backfill and daily collectors coexist. O5 closes with reconciliation, the third workflow. O4 moves to Stage 7 for two reasons: it wraps the finished commands, and the resource sizes it needs (§4.8) come from the measured runs. Apart from these moves, the ranking holds.

- [ ] Stage 1: One real quarter, end to end, locally
      Objective: Download one real archived quarter's master index with an identified User-Agent at ≤3 req/s, keep its raw bytes, and parse it into `sec-index-v1` Parquet on a local machine.
      Outcomes: O1 (one quarter), O3
      Consumes: nothing
      Produces: a local downloader and parser producing `sec-index-v1` rows (§4.5); specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — the raw `master.idx` for the quarter is stored with its SHA-256 and byte count. O3 — Parquet row count equals the index's data-line count, and malformed rows fail closed. The findings file records the measured cost of the real run: bytes, rows, elapsed time, peak memory, request count and observed request rate.
      Leaves out: source manifest, checkpoints and range backfill → Stage 2; generations and active pointer → Stage 3; shared lease → Stage 5; Azure services → Stage 7; typed config validation, alerts and runbooks → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Checkpointed backfill with replay
      Objective: Backfill a configured quarter range from a durable source manifest with content-addressed raw storage, and reprocess stored inputs on a parser change.
      Outcomes: O1, O6
      Consumes: Stage 1's downloader and parser
      Produces: source, snapshot, workset-binding, processing and attempt records (§4.5); `discover`/`collect`/`transform` commands over immutable worksets (§4.1)
      Exit: O1 — a backfill interrupted mid-range resumes and reuses completed members, and its report separates complete, pending and failed units. O6 — a parser-version change rebuilds observations with zero SEC requests, and golden fixtures cover the formats in the chosen range (§4.6).
      Leaves out: generations and active pointer → Stage 3; Table Storage and ADLS backing → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: Versioned quarter publication
      Objective: Publish each affected quarter as an immutable generation, with a manifest and change report, behind a conditionally updated active pointer.
      Outcomes: O9
      Consumes: Stage 2's manifest records and observations
      Produces: a `publish` command; quarter-publication records; generation layout (§4.5, §4.6)
      Exit: O9 — the §6 Publication tests pass: under injected crashes, readers see only complete generations, and competing publishers cannot lose an update.
      Leaves out: withdrawal gate → Stage 6; Table Storage pointer backing → Stage 7
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 4: Daily ingestion and catch-up
      Objective: Discover and ingest daily indexes from the handoff date, catching up across missed runs and quarter boundaries.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stages 2–3's commands, manifest and publication
      Produces: the daily workflow and its discovery boundary (§4.2)
      Exit: O2 — the §6 Discovery and coverage tests pass, and a real catch-up from a past handoff date publishes, with baseline overlap deduplicated and `no_new_sources` reported for valid empty listings.
      Leaves out: shared lease → Stage 5; ADF schedule → Stage 7
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 5: One shared SEC request budget
      Objective: Make every collector acquire one renewable lease and one request budget before any SEC access, with daily work given priority.
      Outcomes: O8
      Consumes: Stages 2 and 4's collectors
      Produces: the lease-based collector coordination (§4.3)
      Exit: O8 — the §6 Access tests pass: concurrent collectors never overlap, retries count toward the budget, and lease loss halts requests.
      Leaves out: Azure Storage lease backing in production → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Reconciliation with gated withdrawals
      Objective: Refresh supported quarters on the shared commands, apply safe changes, and gate closed-quarter removals behind hash-bound approval.
      Outcomes: O7, O10, O5
      Consumes: Stages 3–5
      Produces: the reconciliation workflow; withdrawal-approval records (§4.4, §4.5)
      Exit: O7 — the §6 Reconciliation tests pass. O10 — a candidate that removes keys stays `awaiting_approval` until an approval names its hash. O5 — backfill, daily and reconciliation run the same four commands, differing only in source selection.
      Leaves out: approval runbook and alerting → Stage 8
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 7: Azure deployment with triggers disabled
      Objective: Deploy the shared worker image under ADF orchestration with managed identities and versioned infrastructure, and run the smoke test and replay (§7 steps 2–5).
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: Stages 1–6; ADR and spec accepted (§7 step 1)
      Produces: `infra/azure/sec-edgar-ingest/` with a pinned image digest (§4.9); the smoke-test record
      Exit: O4 — the §6 Orchestration and Integration tests pass on isolated resources, and the §7 step 4 smoke test records bytes, rows, elapsed time, peak memory, image digest and request rate. All production triggers remain disabled.
      Leaves out: trigger enablement, alerts and runbooks → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Configuration review and scheduled operation
      Objective: Validate configuration before I/O, add alerts and runbooks, run the baseline campaign, and enable schedules (§7 steps 6–9).
      Outcomes: O11
      Consumes: Stage 7's deployment
      Produces: `conf/sec-edgar-ingest.yaml`, alerts (§4.7), `docs/runbooks/` (§8), the release record
      Exit: O11 — invalid configurations from §5 are refused before any external I/O. The baseline campaign report shows no silent gaps, and observed scheduled daily and reconciliation runs match their durable reports.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans

## Stage-spec stamp

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the
> stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, run the SKILL.md §6 rubric over O1–O11, with evidence per verdict (implementing stage and plan, Deviation notes, deferred_items entries). Every numbered spec requirement (R1–R11) is cited by an outcome's `Spec` cell, so none starts out unmet. Unmet outcomes exit as a new stage, or as a deferral with a written reason.
